items.title: Sheryl Bailey interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 24, 2023
items.q: he had the thing about the Segovia scales

ctx.x: And he said that he used to copy plans out of the New York Times Sunday Real Estate section and he liked to plan stuff. “When I play a piece of music I usually arrange it and think of a concept for it.”

Um hum. Yeah. He definitely — I think he considers himself an arranger, I mean and an amazing arranger. I mean I met him when I was a teenager and that was a great time. He came to Pittsburgh through the Handyman, he was one of the great guitarists and stuff. But he had the thing about the Segovia scales, which are really — they move up on each string. So there’s kind of two ways you could play — you could play what we call in hand position and a grip, or you could play up each string. And so seeing him present…

that was so influential in how I saw the guitar, which I credit to that moment of crossing paths with him. And then fast forward when I moved to New York and I hung out with him and took some lessons. And Gene was always so welcoming of me anytime I came by to sit in with him and introduce me to people. He was just so generous. But anyway, that’s what I studied with him was arranging standards. And I learned so much, I mean stuff that I share with all my students and stuff that I’m still working on all the time.
